summary:
Blue Planet Radio is a browser-based Earth Information Jukebox that lets anyone hear our planet's data. It turns real NASA observations – FIRMS VIIRS wildfires, POWER rainfall, JPL MUR sea-surface temperature, GISS GISTEMP global temperature, and Earth Information Center and GIBS imagery – into live, rule-based sound, so people can notice patterns by listening as well as looking. Fires crackle faster as radiative power rises, rain falls denser as precipitation increases, ocean heat bends a low drone, and 145 years of global temperature become a melody.

Five chapters – a Frame Sonifier, an Explore Earth globe, a Data Jukebox with 17 climate stories and A/B ear comparison, Sonic Quest learning missions, and a Science transparency page – work fully in English and Bangla.

This matters because climate data is mostly shared as color maps and charts, which shuts out many of the 2.2 billion people living with vision impairment and many first-time learners. Blue Planet Radio makes sound a first-class way to explore science, with screen-reader tables, a 2D map alternative, keyboard control, high contrast and reduced motion. All audio is generated in the browser with the Web Audio API.
details:
Blue Planet Radio – "Hear Earth Change." An independent team entry for NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026, not an official NASA product.

Full 4-minute video: https://youtu.be/RoJC-XWyXTk
Live app: https://blue-planet-radio.vercel.app
Source code: https://github.com/sample77-ctrl/BLUE-PLANET-RADIO

WHAT IT DOES

Blue Planet Radio is an Earth Information Jukebox. It turns real NASA Earth observations into sound that is generated live in the browser. Each data value controls pitch, loudness, rhythm, timbre or stereo position, so anyone, including blind and low-vision users, can hear where fires burn hottest, where rain falls heaviest, where the ocean is warmest, and how the climate has changed since 1880.

WHY IT MATTERS

  • WHO reports that at least 2.2 billion people live with a near or distance vision impairment.
  • NASA found that 2024 was the warmest year on record, 1.28°C above the 1951–1980 average.
  • Climate evidence this important should not be visual-only. Our app makes listening a real way to analyze data, not just background music.

HOW IT WORKS – FIVE CHAPTERS

1. Frames – EIC Visual Frame Sonifier

  • A playhead scans NASA Earth Information Center images from west to east: the greenhouse gas warming index, ocean heat content since 1957, El Niño crop-yield forecasts and GEOS global weather.
  • Pixel height → pentatonic note, brightness → loudness, color → timbre (warm colors sound buzzy, cool colors sound soft).
  • Before/After mode compares two images by ear.

2. Explore Earth – Hear the Planet This Week

  • A 3D globe with Map and List alternatives plays three NASA layers:
    • FIRMS VIIRS fire radiative power → crackles
    • POWER MERRA-2 daily rain → droplets
    • JPL MUR sea-surface temperature anomaly → low drone
  • Longitude pans the sound left and right, and latitude sets its spatial elevation.
  • A "What you are hearing" panel names each sound in plain text, and "Hear the change" plays the week day by day.
  • Country search covers 174+ countries.


168 real NASA observations on one day. Every pin is a sound, and the side panel explains each one in words.

3. Data Jukebox – 17 Climate Stories

  • NASA GISTEMP global temperature (1880–2025)
  • NOAA Mauna Loa CO₂ (1959–2025)
  • NSIDC Arctic sea ice (1979–2025)
  • Ocean heat, weekly fire peaks and Bangladesh monsoon rainfall
  • Each value maps to a G3–G5 pentatonic note, and year-to-year change sets 1–6 rhythm pulses.
  • A/B mode plays an older period in one ear and a recent period in the other.


2025 sounds as E5 (659 Hz): 1.19°C above the 1951–1980 average.

4. Sonic Quest – Learning Missions

  • Amazon Wildfire: find FIRMS fire hotspots by their crackle and put them out.
  • Bengal Monsoon: collect POWER rain data in Sylhet and rescue animals.
  • Pacific Submarine: use sonar and plant MUR sea-temperature buoys.
  • Orbital Station: align four observation beams to play the 145-year climate melody.
  • Players can also use Earth DJ Studio, Free Roam, badges and certificates.


Every mission plays real NASA data. Players listen first, then act.

5. About the Science & Harmonium

  • Every formula, unit and sampling limit is explained openly.
  • An educational harmonium maps notes to historical years. It is a learning aid, not a forecast.
















SONIFICATION RULES

  • Wildfires: fire radiative power 5–800 MW (log scale) → 4–20 crackles/sec, 800–3000 Hz filter
  • Rain: mm/day (square-root scale) → 3–18 drops/sec, 340–700 Hz
  • Ocean heat: SST anomaly → 110 Hz drone that shifts pitch with warm or cool values
  • Climate stories: value → G3–G5 pentatonic note; yearly change → 1–6 pulses
  • Images: pixel height → pitch, brightness → loudness, color → timbre

ACCESSIBILITY & INCLUSION

  • Full English and Bangla interface with Bengali numerals and Web Speech narration
  • Screen-reader List view and a 2D Map alternative to the 3D globe
  • Keyboard shortcuts (press ?), high contrast, reduced motion and stereo/spatial audio modes

TOOLS & TECHNOLOGY

  • Frontend: React 19, TypeScript, Vite, Tailwind CSS 4
  • 3D & maps: Three.js, D3-geo
  • Audio: Web Audio API (no plugins, no server)
  • Hosting: Vercel
  • Build scripts bundle normalized NASA snapshots for fast, reliable loading. NASA POWER and GIBS can also be queried live, and the interface labels which data is bundled and which is live.

QUALITY

  • 436 unit tests in 50 files pass
  • 24 Playwright browser tests pass
  • 20 axe-core accessibility scans show 0 violations
  • Lint is clean; the main bundle is 137.5 kB gzip

HONEST LIMITS

  • Atlas layers use a 2–7 October 2026 snapshot, not continuous streaming.
  • The rain map highlights the 48 wettest points of a global grid.
  • The harmonium is illustrative, not a forecast.

SI DISCLOSURE

  • We used Claude (Anthropic) to help write and debug code, draft documentation and translate the interface into Bangla.
  • The Commander Nova character and some mission card illustrations are SI-generated and carry a visible "AI-generated" label.
  • The optional in-app science chat uses an AI language model and falls back to pre-written snapshots when offline.
  • All sonification audio is synthesized live from data by the Web Audio API and is not AI-generated.
  • Every NASA data mapping was designed and checked by our team.




    Note: A full 240-second video has been provided to help you understand the project more clearly.
